Q1_has_either_adapter_forked_a_core_skil.answer: NO in the repository, YES on disk after --global
Q1_has_either_adapter_forked_a_core_skil.evidence: diffed all four file pairs directly. setup/opencode/{install,uninstall}.{sh,ps1} are the setup/codex/ files under a codex -> opencode token substitution and nothing else: install.sh 84 diff lines, install.ps1 68, uninstall.sh 34, uninstall.ps1 38, every one a branding, fence-marker, owner-token or usage string. Neither installer embeds skill text - the four heredocs write AGENTS.md fence content, runtime.json, PLANNING.md and README.md, never a SKILL.md. Both copy the routing skill from platforms/shared/agent-skills/advanced-planning. BUT --global runs ap_rewrite_call_sites (sed) over the copied markdown, so the installed global copy no longer matches the shared source
Q1_has_either_adapter_forked_a_core_skil.drift_already_present: install.ps1 is 507 lines for codex and 510 for opencode; the three extra lines are a comment block present only in the opencode copy. The pair is therefore no longer a pure substitution, which is drift in a 607-line wholesale duplication that nothing enforces

Q2_is_the_human_approval_gate_real.answer: NO on either host - it is prose the model may simply not obey
Q2_is_the_human_approval_gate_real.evidence: the gate is an instruction in SKILL.md and references/manual-review.md. No installer hook, permission or runtime predicate refuses decomposition without a phase_approved record, and setup/codex and setup/opencode both install no host config at all. manual-review.md:39 states 'No absent hook may silently approve or skip', which is precisely what happens
Q2_is_the_human_approval_gate_real.corroborating_measurement: loop-004-4 measured this from the other side: the codex host DID stop at the gate unprompted, so the prose works when obeyed. That is evidence of compliance, not of enforcement

findings.title: --global never writes skill-ownership.json, so a global uninstall deletes the shared skill the other adapter is using
findings.evidence: write_ownership is defined at setup/codex/install.sh:304 and called exactly ONCE, at line 597, on the project path. The global branch opens at line 360 and ends with exit 0 at line 424 - before 597. Identical line numbers in setup/opencode/install.sh. Uninstall calls process_ownership at lines 266/269 regardless of mode (uninstall_from is invoked for global at :336 and project at :343), and with no registry the owners list is empty, so the decision falls to 'elif skill_exists: REMOVE'
findings.consequence: codex --global then opencode --global: uninstalling either removes ~/.agents/skills/advanced-planning while the other adapter is still installed. The ownership mechanism that exists to prevent exactly this is never engaged on the global path
findings.why_round_1_missed_it: setup/opencode/install.sh was one of the four files the truncated envelope dropped entirely

findings.title: CI job 2 imports a module that no longer exists - introduced inside the reviewed range
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:51 reads 'from platforms.python.tests.minischema import validate, UnsupportedKeyword'. At the base fbc559b that path EXISTED and the import was correct. Commit c8057d2, which IS inside fbc559b..c6f7a53, moved it to platforms/python/minischema.py. ci.yml was touched once in range (05918a5) for an unrelated reason and the import was not updated. At tip c6f7a53 platforms/python/tests/minischema.py is absent and every other importer uses the new path
findings.attribution_correction: the controller first judged this pre-existing, on a git log that returned c8057d2 without checking whether c8057d2 was in range. It is. The reviewer's attribution was right and the controller's softening of it was wrong
findings.consequence: CI job 2 fails with ModuleNotFoundError the first time any of these branches is pushed. It has never fired because none has been pushed - so the CI gate this very loop built is itself unexercised
findings.not_on_main: main (c7efad6) has neither minischema path and its ci.yml has no minischema reference at all, so merging loop-003-hostneutral does NOT carry this defect. fbc559b is self-consistent

findings.title: Both uninstallers delete the shared launcher unconditionally, ignoring the other adapter
findings.evidence: setup/codex/uninstall.sh:295-305 removes bin/ap.py and runtime.json with no ownership check, immediately after the KEEP/REMOVE loop that IS ownership-aware. Same block in the opencode copy
findings.consequence: project dual-install: skills correctly survive via skill-ownership.json while the runtime they call is deleted, so every surviving command fails at exit 3. Ownership protects skill directories only

findings.title: A third-party skill's registration is destroyed when no approved skill has owners left
findings.evidence: in uninstall.sh's process_ownership, any_remaining is initialised False at line 196 and set True only at line 214, inside 'for skill in approved_skills'. Line 241 then reads 'elif not any_remaining and confirmed and os.path.exists(owner_file): os.remove(owner_file)'. A non-approved skill with live owners never sets the flag, so the whole registry file is deleted with its entry in it. The if-branch at 221 does carefully preserve non-approved entries - which makes the else-branch an inconsistency, not a deliberate choice

findings.title: The OpenCode README asserts the opposite of the contract it ships
findings.evidence: platforms/opencode/README.md:79-85 states 'OpenCode can commit' and 'Worker: Can stage, commit, and manage git state as needed'. The worker prompt BOTH adapters install - references/worker-prompt.md Hard Contract (a) - states 'NEVER commit ... it never issues git commit, git add, or git reset'. platforms/codex/README.md at the same lines is consistent with the contract
findings.why_it_is_worse_than_a_doc_bug: the README is factually correct about capability - opencode is the one runtime in this fleet that CAN commit from a linked worktree - and wrong about policy. A reader gets no cue that it contradicts the installed contract. The operator reads one, the worker obeys the other

findings.title: The POSIX collision check does not recurse; the PowerShell one does
findings.evidence: setup/codex/install.sh:211 iterates 'for _src_file in "$_src"/*' - top level only. setup/codex/install.ps1:119 uses Get-ChildItem -File -Recurse, and the copy at :54 is -Recurse. So references/ is installed but never collision-checked by the shell installer
findings.consequence: the SHA refusal story does not hold for the reference prompts, which are exactly where the human gate and the Hard Contract live

findings.title: The differential tests can pass vacuously - this phase's defect class inside the test suite
findings.evidence: test_adapter_lifecycle.py test_removal_counts_agree parses counts out of installer stdout with a helper that returns None when the line is not found, then asserts count_sh == count_ps1. If the 'Done. N path(s) removed, M kept.' wording ever changes, both sides return None and the test passes having compared nothing. test_registry_contents_agree is worse: it discards both _run_script return codes and treats FileNotFoundError as None on both sides, so two uninstallers that failed to run at all compare equal
findings.note: this is the phase's central defect exactly - a check whose subject is a string it parsed, with no guard that the parse succeeded - sitting in the suite meant to catch it

findings.title: No test compares the two adapters to each other
findings.evidence: test_adapter_lifecycle.py parametrises over (adapter, language), so each adapter is exercised independently and TestLanguagesAgree compares sh against ps1 WITHIN one adapter. Nothing compares codex against opencode, and nothing installs both. The CI job named 'Audit install-layer drift' checks platforms/claude-code and core/schemas against .claude/ - a different axis entirely
findings.consequence: 607 duplicated lines per file across four files, with drift already present (F-Q1), and no guard on the duplication

findings.title: Installers print a pointer to a README that does not exist
findings.evidence: setup/codex/install.sh:607 prints 'See setup/codex/README.md'. setup/codex/ and setup/opencode/ each contain exactly four files, all scripts. The docs live at platforms/codex/README.md

fleet_findings.title: herdr pane run silently failed to deliver 3 of 4 review launches
fleet_findings.evidence: fanout wrote .launched naming all four panes. Round 1 cursor ran; round 1 agy, round 2 cursor and round 2 agy did not - their panes were alive but had painted nothing, no process existed, and stderr-agy.log had never even been created by the redirect. Running the generated run-*.sh scripts directly worked first time in every case
fleet_findings.defect_class: .launched records the intent string, not a verified fact - the same shape this phase has now hit nine times. A launcher that cannot report a failed launch is not a launcher
fleet_findings.workaround: fanout --no-panes runs the reviewer directly and worked

fleet_findings.title: A second model agreed on the conclusion while fabricating the citations
fleet_findings.evidence: Qwen located F1 independently but cited setup/opencode/install.sh:326 for the global exit and :445 for write_ownership. Line 326 is 'try:' inside a Python block and line 445 is a say statement; the true values are 424 and 597, which is what the controller measured from disk and what cursor cited
fleet_findings.why_it_matters: cross-model agreement raised confidence in the CONCLUSION while one model's EVIDENCE was invented. Consensus is not verification; only the disk settled it. This is the argument for the standing rule that a reviewer's summary is never taken as evidence
